text:
support-jen: FYI customer (ACME) reporting sharp p95/p99 regression starting ~03:10 UTC. P95 from ~120ms to ~1.1s, p99 up to ~2.4s. They saw a lot of 429s and a handful of 503s. Ticket: #ACME-487. Customer included request_id: rq_0a1b2c and logs attached.

support-jen: Quick paste from their logs: 
```
time=2026-03-16T03:12:03Z level=warn msg=\"queue_depth=312 max_workers=64 inflight=58\" request_id=rq_0a1b2c route=/v1/generate tenant=acme
time=2026-03-16T03:12:03Z level=error msg=\"handler_timeout\" request_id=rq_0a1b2c backend=worker-7
```

support-jen: Customer says repro is intermittent but easy to hit when they burst 200 concurrent small requests. Provided a quick repro: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"token test"}' &
done
```

eng-oncall-max: looking into it now. Can someone grab the ingress/admit controller metrics around 03:05-03:20 UTC? Specifically admit_queue_length, admit_rejections, max_inflight_per_tenant and worker_queue_depth. @eng-runtime-aria can you tail worker-7 logs for that window?

eng-runtime-aria: tailing logs now, pulling traces for rq_0a1b2c. I can see repeated KV cache misses + larger-than-normal batches forming, then worker GC spikes. Attaching sample scrubbed trace: 
```
[trace] recv -> batcher(wait 250ms) -> batch size 48 -> worker-7 start -> cpu spin 800ms -> timeout fallback -> retry -> response 1200ms
```

sre-lin: This reads like admission-control + batching interaction. Burst causes batcher to accumulate many small requests (to hit throughput) which increases latency for p99. Also worker-7 shows long GC cycles at that time. Immediate mitigations: 
- reduce batch_wait_ms temporarily from 250 to 80 for affected pool
- cap max_batch_size to 24
- enforce per-tenant max_inflight=16 (customer currently at 32)
- enable fast-fail path for small requests (short-circuit heavy quantization ops)

eng-oncall-max: Agree. I'll push a canary to reduce batch_wait and max_batch_size on the non-prod canary pool, then promote if stable. Also we should update admission controller to short-circuit heavy batching for tenants with burst patterns.

eng-runtime-aria: Repro script I used to simulate: 
```
wrk -t12 -c200 -d30s --latency --header "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" --connection-close \ 
  --script=post.lua https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
post.lua fires many small payloads (~60-100 tokens) with no prefix cache. That reproduces the p99 spike locally.

deploy-bot: deploy-1234: canary patch applied to pool-canary-3 (batch_wait_ms=80, max_batch_size=24) by eng-oncall-max at 03:22 UTC :rocket:

eng-oncall-max: Canary looks good after 5 minutes: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 down to ~650ms on canary. Rolling patch to one additional pool and enabling tenant-level max_inflight enforcement for ACME.

support-jen: Notified customer of temporary mitigation and asked them to test. Asked them to avoid synchronous bursts >50 concurrent requests for next 4 hours while we finish rollout.

product-maria: Please add a short follow-up with postmortem-like notes: root cause hypothesis (bursty tenant + default aggressive batching + worker GC), mitigations (batch config, per-tenant inflight cap), and customer impact. We'll want to evaluate a longer-term fix: adaptive batching, request classification to prefer low-latency path for small requests, or tenant-side QoS.

sre-lin: Agreed. Long-term actions I propose: 
- add admit-controller signal for shaping (burst token bucket per-tenant)
- implement adaptive batch_wait that shrinks when queue depth rises above threshold
- autoscaler: detect persistent high queue_depth and spin up warm workers (reduce GC churn by avoiding cold worker reuse)
- add a routing policy to put latency-sensitive tenants on a low-latency pool by default

eng-runtime-aria: I'll open up a runbook PR with exact CLIs we used and the wrk script + env variables. Also will attach the logs and the canary dashboards.

support-jen: Customer confirmed improvement at 03:35 UTC, p99 acceptable on their side. They still want a timeline for permanent fix. I've linked product & eng owners.

product-maria: Thanks. Schedule a short postmortem + prioritization in next planning; tag me.

support-jen: Closing loop with customer now, will keep thread updated if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
